identity: Arabic Wikipedia encyclopedic article on al-'imara al-bina'iyya (Constructivist architecture). Structure: a lead paragraph carrying a bare footnote marker (1) and two parenthesised language glosses (bi-al-injliziyya: Constructivist Architecture / bi-al-rusiyya: konstruktivistskoy arkhitektury); a second lead paragraph on origins and the 1920 Realistic Manifesto; a bare section heading al-tarikh standing alone between two <NL>; then two long expository art-history paragraphs on Italian Futurism's impact on Russia, Tatlin versus Malevich, and the Vesnin/Ladovsky split that produced OSA. Compiled/translated reference prose - doctrine register SS-L (encyclopedic), governed by SS-B rules. Not narrative, not memoir, no dialogue.
law: The sentence here is the punctuation unit of the source article, not the semantic period: every '.' and ':' and most ',' that closed a unit became a boundary. Target rhythm 12-20 tokens (LAW 6, SS-L band); per LAW 0 I cut at every coin flip, because my documented bias is 5:1 under-cutting and my precision was never the problem. Operative rules: LAW 1 at full strength - wa + a finite clause bearing a NEW argument (new subject NP, new object, new predicate nominal) is a new sentence, while wa merely joining nouns/adjectives/PPs inside one predication never cuts; SS-L warns specifically that wa-tashmul / wa-hiya appositive-continuation clauses are exactly what I keep wrongly absorbing, and wa-dammat, wa-tajma', wa-utliqat, wa-kana here are that same shape. LAW 2 - fa- resumptive openers (fa-fi 'am 1913) start sentences, but a fa- required by an amma...fa- frame, or standing as the apodosis of bi-al-raghm min anna, is grammatically bound and never cuts. B2 - fi hin, hayth, kama open segments. B3 - illa anna does not. LAW 4 - a trailing relative or adjunct carrying no wa belongs to its main clause; but wa+alladhi / wa+allati is a LAW 1 head, not a LAW 4 tail. LAW 3 - parallel repetition cuts. A colon is a boundary (LAW 0 corollary, A4), which decides the two language glosses and the appositive naming of the two tendencies. <NL> is always immediately preceded by a boundary and never itself carries one.
reasoning: Register first (LAW 6): the opening 200 tokens are dated reference prose with named actors, so I set the band at 12-20 and landed at ~12.2 average - deliberately at the low edge, because LAW 0 says my failure is recall, not precision. Hard sites in order. (1) @3 bi-al-injliziyya and @6 bi-al-rusiyya: the source is the standard gloss '(bi-al-injliziyya: Constructivist Architecture)', i.e. a colon, and the LAW 0 corollary plus A4 make a colon a boundary. This produces the absurd-looking segments 'al-'imara al-bina'iyya 1 bi-al-injliziyya' and 'Constructivist Architecture bi-al-rusiyya' - but A1/A2 establish that this gold cuts inside 'Robert L. Rothstein' and inside 'hindawi.org'. Reconstruct the ink, not the meaning. I did NOT cut at @5 or @8: a closing parenthesis is not in the mark set. med. (2) @17 al-haditha and @28 al-ula: the two lead commas. @28 is doubly supported - wa-dammat is precisely the wa-tashmul shape SS-L says I absorb and the gold cuts. (3) @54 al-'imara before wa-qad zaharat awwal wathiqa: this leaves a 5-token segment, below band, but wa-qad + a brand-new subject NP is the strongest LAW 1 configuration there is, and C2 licenses short segments. I cut rather than protect the band. hi. (4) @66 1920, @194 Bitirsburgh, @258 hurra: three instances of one shape - an asyndetic post-nominal clause (dammat khams mabadi'; sharaka fihi 'adad; yatimm ta'liquha) sitting behind a comma in the source. I cut all three for internal consistency, and each welded alternative overshoots the band (24-35 tokens). T3 says this discriminator is still a hypothesis, so all three are med, not hi. (5) @80 al-tayyar before ma'a al-ta'kid: a trailing PP. LAW 4 argues weld, but K4 licenses an emphatic trailing PP as its own segment and welding gives 27 tokens. Cut, med. (6) @123 and @507, both illa anna, both left uncut per B3 - and here B3 is structurally confirmed rather than merely observed, since each is the apodosis of a fronted bi-al-raghm min anna and literally cannot open a sentence. That is two more data points for Tension T1, and they suggest the T1 asymmetry is real rather than accidental: ghayr anna is a free adversative head, illa anna is the bound second half of a concessive frame. (7) @288 al-subrmati before wa-alladhi, and @529 1924 before wa-allati: LAW 4 would weld a trailing relative, but the wa is a LAW 1 trigger and welding gives 36- and 43-token units. I cut both. The control is @525, where 'allati assasaha 'am 1924' carries no wa and I did NOT cut - so the discriminator I am proposing is: bare relative welds, wa+relative heads. (8) @224 andhak before al-subrmatiyya wa-al-bina'iyya: I read a colon naming the two tendencies, yielding a 2-token segment (C2 permits this). The control is @352/@353, where 'huma Aliksandr Fiznin wa-Nikulay Ladufiski' has an explicit copula huma that makes a colon unnecessary, and there I did NOT cut. Both sites are decided by the same test - colon present, or copula present - which is exactly why I am confident they should disagree. (10) @318 khass before wa-khassatan: NOT cut. wa-khassatan fi tasmim al-mulsaqat has no predicate and introduces no new argument, so LAW 1's phrase-level exception governs, and the resulting 20-token unit is in band. This is the one place I resisted LAW 0, and I did it on an explicit rule rather than on instinct. Accepting four over-band units is the price of not inventing joints where the source had no mark - LAW 0 tells me to cut at coin flips, not to manufacture boundaries at non-sites.
